svg.aria-label: How to write ા: one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
svg.title: Writing ા
svg.desc: 2 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ા (gujarati), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/1_ka.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the aa sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>. Source note on variation: In the template for કા, and in all 32 consonant rows whose consonant keeps its bare outline, ા is one pen-down run that starts at the top of the bar, draws it straight down, and ends in a short foot to the right at the baseline. t30apps' Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice, already cited for આ, draws its trailing ā stem the same way: after the body, down into a matching foot. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: 55 of its 81 stored prototypes of the aa sign (68%) are one stroke, and 98% of those move downward. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer.
